title: There’s a lot to like
body:
+ Can try out full app for free with 3 habits
+ Lots of features, including stats & timers
+ Great data privacy (no data collected)
+ No ads
+ No need to create user account 
+ No subscription 🥳🎉
+ Very reasonable one-time purchase price

You can get full statistics with a calendar view and completion rates, but there are also nice features that not all habit trackers have : you can track habits that are multiple times a day (e.g. glasses of water) and set multiple timers (e.g. for workouts, or to be reminded several times a day).

The only downside for me is the design.
It’s a matter of taste of course, but I’d prefer more color and the option to have a cleaner look with less text in the habit list. Presently I’m using other habit trackers that have fewer features but are more visually appealing to me.

Wish list:
• More colorful design options, e.g. optional background color instead of just the vertical red/yellow/green stripe 
• Ability to choose different color for each habit
• Option to display less text info under habit name
• Apple Watch! I’d be very happy to pay extra for it as an in-app purchase (but only as a one-time purchase, please!)

I think this app has a lot going for it, so I purchased the premium version because I want to support the excellent privacy and pricing policies! I hope the developer will keep up the good work!

title: Affordable but Lacking
body:
A good effort, I can see the developer means well. Unfortunately, this app is missing some basic functionality that is essential for an app such as a habit/routine tracker. 

I would save the couple bucks and find an app that’s more developed and has more active support. Nothing in this app has improved in the few months I’ve used it. 

Example of missing functionality:
- Unable to view tasks in a routine without editing the routine, or starting the whole routine and having to go through each item one at a time. There’s no way to simply say “I did this thing but not the others”
- Default view is the only view, there’s no way to see only what’s currently due. The default view shows all tasks for the whole day, with no way to change the default filter. 
- Badge app icon shows number of items for the whole day, not the number of items pending completion now - again, no way to customize. 

For a habit tracker, the lack of ability to customize preferences or be presented with items the way I’d like to be, is very disappointing. Save your dollars.

Edit: The development team reached out and stated they are working on adding these features. In return, I am working on taking down my negative review. I expect they’ll both be completed around the same time.

title: Really Good App
body:
This app has been such a great help! Before using it, I set timers for all the things I needed to remember to do. If I wasn’t able to do the task right then, I would either have to hit “snooze” and have the alarm go off every few minutes until I completed it, or turn the alarm off and hope that I wouldn’t forget to do it when time became available.

With this app, if I have a task come up that I don’t have time for right then, then I can just ignore it and it will notify me how ever often I set it to (usually every hour). Love it! I can also tell it when to start reminding me and when to stop, so I don’t have to worry about getting a reminder after bedtime. 

Another great thing, not only can I set up reminders for things I do frequently - everyday, every other day, once a week - but I can also set up reminders for things that don’t come up that often but I often forget - such as changing the filters on my air conditioner. I have multiple reminders for 3 and 6 months!

I love this app! It gives me the ability to take things off my minds “remember to-do” list and helps me still get them done!

title: This system keeps me functional!
body:
I have ASD and have some executive functioning issues which have been exacerbated during the pandemic. I tried a few other apps to keep me on task/on schedule and found it was too easy for me to ignore them. But this app? This app works! 
1) I love that it’s a widget! I can see what I need to do right from the home screen without having to open the app. That’s super helpful! Because of my EF issues, if I have to seek it out a lot of the time it’s not happening. I can miss notifications, but not if it’s on my Home Screen. 
2) Thank you for %’s and grades. This is how my brain works. Since I’ve put a daily exercise routine as one of my tasks, I’m actually completing it so I can stay at a 90% “grade”. This is the first year I’ve actually stuck out a workout routine because of it! 
3) I can keep track of tasks that are weekly, monthly, etc. Instead of wondering the last time I cleaned out the fridge, I can check the app. I feel like I’m on top of things instead of drowning in a bunch of stuff that needs to be done or hasn’t been done in months since I keep forgetting about it. 
This app has been literally life changing for me. I feel much more in control of my own life and home in ways that I never have before. Thank you so, so much!

title: Great app but a couple suggestions :D
body:
This app is a gem and I really like it worth every penny. I have three small suggestions that I would LOVE to be implemented. 

1. Make it so that tasks that are due at the same time or in the same time frame be able to be sorted in a specific order that stays consistent each time the tasks repeat. (to me this is the most necessary)

For example I have “Brush Teeth” and “Wash Face” both set at morning 7:00 am - 12:00 pm because editing them to the minute is pointless but I would like it if they could always maintain their order ex. “Brush Teeth” first then “Wash Face”

Perhaps you could add a manual sort feature? 
Like when “edit” is clicked show the tasks grouped into time sections ex: 

 ——— 7:00 am - 12:00 pm ———
 • Brush teeth
 • Wash face
 • Brush hair
•——— 7:00 am - 12:00 am ———•
 • Upload to Instagram
 • Clean room
 ——— 9:00 pm - 11:00 pm ———
 • Read 20 pages
 • Write in journal

Notice how the all day task can be manually placed in a certain spot between the specific times and sorted between themselves.
I think some sort of easily identifiable thing should be used so that the user can easily tell which ones are all day tasks are which ones are set time tasks when editing and sorting so that organizing can be easier.

If the sorting of all day tasks between set time tasks is too complex at least allow for sorting between the set time tasks that occur at the same time and all day tasks individually.

2. Let tasks occur multiple times a day at set specific times. 

Allow for, for example, “Brush Teeth” to occur twice a day. Once between 7:00 am - 12:00 pm and another between 8:00 pm - 11:00 pm

This sounds mostly easily to implement as it is just making a task reoccur more frequently and specificity. Instead of just doing it twice a day, you have a set time to do it twice each day. 

3. Implement a select feature.

When “edit” is clicked allow for perhaps a bubble or a box to be checked off beside tasks so that you can easily edit a group of tasks’ time, delete them, change their sound, etc.

This also sounds mostly easy to implement.

That’s all yes I’m asking a lot 😆 but I really do love this app and even if none of this is implemented I’ll continue to use it. 

Thanks for the great app 😄👌

title: Great, Simple, Useful
body:
I’ve been using this app for a while and it’s been going pretty well. It does a very nice job of tracking the daily things that I normally might forget to do, and I really like how it analyzes and displays my progress weekly, monthly, etc. 

One of the best things is that the premium version is only a one time payment of $2.99, which I think is absolutely worth it. Almost every single other app I’ve looked at wants monthly or annual subscriptions that are way more expensive, and none of them are as good.

The only thing I would want to improve on is to be able to sort all of our daily tasks into their own groups instead of having them all listed together. title: Simple to use and very flexible!
body:
I’ve tried a lot of apps to help me improve my habits and manage my routines, but this is the first one that has both flexibility AND simplicity. There is a little bit of a learning curve to setting up habits with certain settings, but once they are set up, the app is super simple in day to day use. One thing I really like is the ability to easily set up timed routines. I use these for my morning and evening routines to stay focused and get things done in way less time. By setting a certain number of minutes for each task, I am able to stay on track and get a list of tasks done in an hour that would likely take me 90 minutes if a timer wasn’t running. 

I’d like to see is the ability to override certain app settings on a habit by habit basis. For instance, I have to file certain reports to the IRS on a monthly basis that are due by the 15th. I set a habit to have me do it monthly on the 5th. If I don’t do it by midnight on the 5th, it marks the habit as incomplete and it disappears until next month. For daily habits, like flossing my teeth for example, that’s appropriate. But for monthly tasks it’s often hard to predict the exact day you’ll be able to do something. A checkbox to tell the app to keep it active until complete would be great. 

It would also be great to be able to “push back” habits by an hour, several hours, a day, or several days so that something that’s in the red can be moved down the list a bit instead of skipping them completely.

body:
HabitHub is one of a few apps that allows you to set a time of day in which you are to complete the task. I like that the app will remind you hourly to complete each task — a single reminder at a set time, which is all many other apps offer, is not useful to me.

title: May Very Well Be the Best
body:
Like other reviewers, I've tried (and wasted money on) a lot of other apps in hopes of finding the one that best helped me track and complete my habitual rituals. This one is the best of all the ones I've tried. Its simplicity is disarming at first, but is what ultimately wins the day. Also, support is quickly responsive. 

A few suggestions I have:

1) Marking an item as Done has been a little tricky for me. It's all in the touch for swiping, and I'm an experienced swiper, but find that many times the item disappears before I can choose my swiped option, which causes me to freak out that I might have deleted it, but always I've been gladdened to see that it was indeed marked Done and moved down to its appropriate place in the list. Not sure if sensitivity can be coded in but this feels a little too sensitive to me. Alternatively, there's the option to tap the Done button, but it's so close to the Info button that I end up opening Info for the item as many times as I mark one Done. Since tapping the item brings up its Info anyway, I'd vote to remove the Info button altogether. 

2) Would love the ability to add a short note or link to an item. For instance, I have say a monthly task of "Computer Maintenance" and an associated Evernote note with all the subtasks. It would be great to have the link for the Evernote note right with the task (though I realize that may negate the simple design), rather than me having to hunt down the note. 

3) The scheduling options are flexible and handy, but I couldn't figure out how to schedule something I need to do every OTHER Sunday. Would be great to have a little more scheduling customization. As it stands, I'll keep the bi-weekly type things in my calendar, but I'd really like to use the calendar less for these every day/week/month types of tasks. 

Otherwise, it's a phenomenal app and one that is surprisingly perfect for this sort of thing in spite - or because - of it's simplicity!
